newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Credit Suisse strategy based on broad EMU.
newsitem.headline: Credit Suisse strategy based on broad EMU.

text.p: Credit Suisse recommended Swiss franc-based investors expand their southern European bond holdings in the expectation that Europe's single currency will be soft and include several founding members.
"The chances of a broad EMU (economic and monetary union) have clearly risen and this is our favoured scenario," the bank's economic research department wrote in its latest investment policy report.

"The option of a postponement cannot be ruled out as well. We are aligning our asset allocation more towards a broad EMU. That is why we are expanding our exposure to southern European countries, especially Italy."
It recommended lire and peseta bond funds.

It said low inflationary pressure around the world still offered good support for bond prices. It saw weak bond performance in core European countries where an economic upturn is expected next year, but said U.S. bonds were attractive given an expected cooling of the U.S. economy in 1998.
British bonds are also attractive for EMU reasons, it added.
It said the environment for shares was still positive, but added it had reduced shares to neutral from overweight because a consolidation could not be excluded after recent strong gains.
"European exchanges still remain our favourites," it said.

Credit Suisse said foreign currencies had a neutral share in its asset allocation policy. "Prospects for a broad EMU support the dollar, pound and Swiss franc. We weight the dollar neutral overall. Within Europe, the southern axis is overweighted, the mark underweighted," it said.
